prompt: Mid-case: The client's profit fell 20%. You've found that revenue is flat and that COGS rose 25% because bean prices doubled. You haven't looked at labor costs yet. Which is the best summary?

options.text: So far: both beans and labor drove the decline, and revenue fell too. Next I'd look at pricing.
options.feedback: This claims findings the analysis hasn't shown. Summarize only what you've established.

options.text: So far: revenue is flat, and profit fell mainly because bean prices doubled, pushing COGS up 25%. The client also opened two stores in 2019. Next I'd check labor to see if it adds to the squeeze.
options.feedback: It leads with the answer, but pads it with a fact that doesn't bear on the decision.

options.text: So far: revenue is flat, and profit fell mainly because bean prices doubled, pushing COGS up 25%. We haven't yet looked at labor costs, so next I'd check labor to see if it adds to the squeeze.
options.feedback: Right. It states what is known, with numbers, then what is still open and what comes next.

options.text: So far: costs went up, which hurt profit. Next I'd check labor to see if it adds to the squeeze.
options.feedback: It gives an answer but none of the numbers from the fact sheet to back it.

explanation: Revenue is flat, and profit fell mainly because bean prices doubled, pushing COGS up 25%. A good mid-case summary states what is known with numbers and what comes next, without claiming findings that haven't been tested.

irrelevant_facts: The client also opened two stores in 2019.
